newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian railways ministry plans eurobond in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russian railways ministry plans eurobond in 1997.

text.p: Russia's Railways Ministry plans to issue a government-guaranteed Eurobond in 1997, Minister Anatoly Zaitsev said on Tuesday.
Approval for the issue is still needed from the Finance Ministry and Central Bank, he told a news conference.
"There will be trial issue of a few hundred million dollars. Our further actions will depend on the reaction of the market. It could be up to $2 billion a year," Zaitsev said.
Zaitsev said initial documents for the issue had been drawn up.
"Being realistic, it will be issued next year... I know our bureaucracy will not succeed this year," he said.
The proceeds of the issue will be used to cover operating costs, he said.
Russian railways have not been privatised, although they are grouped in different regional operating companies.
Russia is likely to launch its debut sovereign Eurobond later this month. A roadshow is currently underway in major financial centres to present the issue.

The cities of St Petersburg and Moscow and the Sverdlovsk region around the Urals city of Yekaterinburg, have also expressed interest in issuing Eurobonds. Several big Russian companies, including NK LUKoil and RAO Gazprom, are also talking about coming to market. --Peter Henderson, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
